newsitem.title: UK: UK EMU group argues case for semi-annual coupons.
newsitem.headline: UK EMU group argues case for semi-annual coupons.

text.p: A working group set up by the Bank of England (BOE) said on Wednesday it would recommend keeping semi-annual coupon payments in Britain on debt issues until a better consensus emerged over the best way to harmonise debt under a single European currency.

The group of market practitioners, set up to look at technical issues of a single European currency, saw harmonising coupon frequency as one of the most difficult issues, said John Townend, deputy director of the BOE, speaking at an EMU conference in London.
"The market group considers that semi-annual coupons have several advantages compared to annual coupons," he said.
Annual payments are the norm in many continental European countries,

Semi-annual coupons reduce investors' credit risk on the issue, most institutional investors prefer more regular income, credit exposure on fixed against floating interest rate swaps linked to the bonds is reduced, and the change in the duration of the bond following an interest payment is smaller, he said.
Townend added that the group recognised some investors preferred to receive income annually.

"The market group does not regard complete harmonisation of coupon frequency as necessary although it would lead to greater transparency on different bonds. The market group is therefore recommending maintenance of existing conventions on coupon frequency until a consensus emerges to change them."
